BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Advisory review against Buyer Playbook. Seller's "fair and balanced" characterisation is noted but not accepted. Note the Seller Update and the Disclosure Letter are internally inconsistent in several places (the Letter is candid about what is *not* done; the Update glosses over it) – we should use the Letter's admissions against the Update's positions.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure matches our fallback, but no Amelia Frost written authority identifying this draft exists, so it cannot be accepted.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject all three elements.** Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the "excess only" (deductible) structure is a separate value transfer beyond the headline numbers.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 24 months.** 18 months is our fallback but no Amelia Frost approval has been given.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge qualifier.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright; this is a red-line.** Collapsing title into a 20%/18-month regime leaves us unprotected on the one thing we are actually buying (the shares) and the "simplicity" rationale has no commercial value to us.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; cl 12.3 default that limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise. No fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insert an express, non-waivable fraud carve-out and reverse the cl 12.3 default.** The current drafting would purport to cap and time-bar fraud claims, which is non-negotiable for us and of doubtful enforceability in any event.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sep 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; Letter [1.1]–[1.2]).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject [1.1] and [1.2]; require disclosures to be specific, fair and referenced to the warranty they qualify.** Whole-data-room disclosure converts our DD burden into a warranty waiver and is inconsistent with the Letter's own specific disclosures in sections 2–10.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Cl 8.3 – no claim for any matter of which Buyer or advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that, combined with SPA-N-006, would effectively void the warranty package.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). Letter s.2 admits no final consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied; ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent **and** evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; endeavours standard insufficient.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; make Bluefen a true condition precedent (effective consent + condition evidence) with Buyer satisfaction.** A ~30% customer with a change-control right is material enough that "reasonable endeavours" and an unconditioned paper consent do not protect the price.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). Letter s.3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. Any post-completion release requires irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-completion release; require payout letter, funds-flow repayment and executed releases as Completion deliverables.** Buying a debt-free/cash-free company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still outstanding at Completion is inconsistent with the agreed price basis.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 bonuses "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow. Letter s.5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or demonstrably Seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; add a specific line item (bonuses + on-costs) funded by Seller or deducted from price, with a Seller indemnity for any shortfall.** "A matter for the Seller" without a funding mechanism means the Company (i.e. us) pays post-Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). Letter s.4: IP transfer under cl 7.3 is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 shown open at DD-010 (not bank-verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broadened indemnity covering title/ownership of Project Materials and consequences of non-transfer, while preserving the SOW3 cure (pay and obtain assignment).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted; broaden to cover loss from any defect in title to SOW3 Project Materials, and require a pre-Completion deliverable of either payment receipt + confirmatory assignment or Seller funding of the cure.** The real exposure is ownership of the IP, not the AUD 180,000 fee, and the AUD 180,000 is unverified in either direction.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). Letter s.6: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification status unknown; investigation preliminary; no breach characterisation, no loss figure.
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, completed investigation, ongoing updates to Completion; no assumption either way on breach, harm, notification duty or quantum.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation; add a pre-Completion covenant (preserve logs, complete investigation, report to Buyer) and a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, uncapped by the general regime.** The materiality judgement cannot be made on a preliminary investigation and should not be made by the Seller.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each are "ordinary-course operating costs". Letter s.8 declines to say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment on the facts; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Neither accept nor contest yet; request DD-008/DD-011 contract terms (timing, termination rights, accrual) and reserve position on Debt/Working Capital treatment.** The Seller's two documents contradict each other and the characterisation drives whether this is a completion-accounts item.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3 – any limitation applies to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"; Tax and IP "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment-obligation and covenant claims kept as separate regimes; no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject cl 12.3 default; replace with an express schedule mapping each claim category to its own cap, threshold and period, with specific indemnities and covenants outside Warranty limitations.** The "unless expressly stated otherwise" default is the mechanism by which SPA-N-004, 005, 011, 012 and 016 would all be silently collapsed.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by Company share register at DD-012. Letter s.10 concedes this is the Seller's source and the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal record, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not treat DD-012 as sufficient; obtain ASIC extract, PPSR search, Riverlark security schedule, Seller constitutional/board authority and (if any) prior transfer chain before Completion.** A company-maintained register is exactly what a title warranty is meant to back, not a substitute for it.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled" under the general regime (20% / 18 months / AUD 25k / AUD 250k).
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain OPEN; no assumption of unlimited liability, but no resolution and no folding into the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled" characterisation; respond that Tax and IP terms remain open and are to be negotiated as separate categories (see SPA-N-014).** The Seller is attempting to close these by assertion rather than agreement.

---

### Summary / escalation flags
- **Red lines breached:** SPA-N-004 (title in general regime), SPA-N-005 (no fraud carve-out), SPA-N-007 (constructive-knowledge bar).
- **Items at fallback level but unauthorised:** SPA-N-001 (20% cap), SPA-N-003 (18 months) – do **not** concede without written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft; none exists.
- **Completion-mechanics gaps:** SPA-N-008 (Bluefen), SPA-N-009 (Riverlark), SPA-N-010 (bonuses) – the Disclosure Letter admits each is unresolved; these go to deliverables and funds flow, not just warranties.
- **Need facts, not positions:** SPA-N-011, 012, 013, 015 – request further DD before fixing a number.

Happy to turn this into a mark-up of the Seller Update or an issues list for the next call.
